Human translators assess a translation by how adequately it expresses the meaning of the source sentence on a 0-100 scale. Side-by-side Adequacy Raters see a source sentence with two translations (one supervised, one unsupervised) and rate each on a 6-point scale. Side-by-side Fluency Raters assess the alternative translations (one supervised, one unsupervised) without the source, and rate each on a 6-point scale.
